name: Standard Route

waypoints.name: Tubal Cain Trailhead
waypoints.note: Self-issue wilderness permit at the kiosk; trailhead reached via FR-2870, 12.5 mi past Dungeness Forks Campground.
waypoints.directions: From US 101 across from Sequim Bay State Park, turn west onto Louella Road and go about 0.9 mi, then turn left onto Palo Alto Road. Follow it about 6 mi as it becomes FS Road 28, turn right onto FS Road 2880 (steep, not suited to trailers), pass Dungeness Forks Campground, and stay left onto FS Road 2870 for about 12.5 mi to the Tubal Cain Trailhead at about 3,300 ft. A recreation pass such as the Northwest Forest Pass is required to park.

waypoints.name: Silver Creek footlog crossing
waypoints.note: Trail crosses Silver Creek on a footlog in the forested lower section; reliable flowing water before the trail opens up.
waypoints.directions: Start up the Tubal Cain Trail #840, passing the Silver Creek shelter, and cross Silver Creek on a footlog early in the forested lower section.

waypoints.name: Tull Canyon Trail junction / Tubal Cain Mine
waypoints.note: Unsigned spur angles left to the 1952 B-17 crash site (0.6 mi, +450 ft); old mine adit and tailings visible on the hillside, mine-shaft water runoff is not safe to drink untreated.
waypoints.directions: Climb gently on well-graded trail through forest and rhododendrons high above Copper Creek. At about 3 mi the Tull Canyon Trail #847 doubles back sharply to the left toward the B-17 crash site, and old mine adits show on the hillside; stay on #840 for the Tubal Cain Mine tailings just beyond.

waypoints.name: Buckhorn Lake spur junction
waypoints.note: Signed junction where a faint side trail drops toward Buckhorn Lake; the main Tubal Cain Trail continues on toward Marmot Pass.
waypoints.directions: Continue on #840 past the mine, cross Copper Creek on a log bridge, the last easy water, and switchback up through subalpine meadows toward Buckhorn Pass. Near 5,200 ft, about 5.7 mi from the trailhead, watch for the lightly signed spur to Buckhorn Lake; it is easy to walk past while the main trail carries on toward Marmot Pass.

waypoints.name: Buckhorn Lake basin (avalanche debris flat)
waypoints.note: Established camp area in an open flat about 200 ft above and south of Buckhorn Lake; last reliable camp/water before leaving the trail.
waypoints.directions: Take the spur down to Buckhorn Lake. From the south end of the lake the tread stops: cross the inlet stream where a small waterfall comes in, then follow a faint boot path southwest through avalanche-flattened timber and blowdown to the broad, flat debris bench about 200 ft above the lake.

waypoints.name: Iron-Worthington col
waypoints.note: Off-trail brush and blowdown give way to open scree/talus gaining this saddle between Iron Mountain and Worthington; the west-side gully is the boot-ski descent route back toward Buckhorn Lake.
waypoints.directions: From the bench climb the wide talus and scree gully, trending south and then curving east, breaking treeline near 5,800 ft onto loose rock and light Class 2-3. Angle east and southeast up increasingly loose slopes to the col between Iron Mountain and Worthington at about 6,420 ft. Cairns are sparse, so read the terrain.

waypoints.name: Loose rock band below the summit plateau
waypoints.note: Notoriously rotten, loose Olympic rock on the final scramble through the rock band; test holds and watch for rockfall onto climbers below.
waypoints.directions: From the col, angle northeast up open slopes toward the base of Worthington's summit fin, where the ground steepens into a band of rotten, loose rock. Test every hold and keep the party out of each other's fall line.

waypoints.name: Mount Worthington summit
waypoints.note: Flat, open summit plateau with a ~40-ft Class 3 summit block some parties rope up for; views to Rainier, Baker, Shuksan, and Puget Sound on clear days.
waypoints.directions: For the final Class 3 scramble, step a few feet left of the ridge crest to a short crack about 10 ft high, climb it, then follow the top of the fin to the true summit. Some parties rope up for the exposed summit block.

approach: Start at the Tubal Cain Trailhead (elev. ~3,300 ft, reached via FR 2870/2880), and follow the Tubal Cain Trail #840 (Copper Creek drainage) south. The trail climbs gently through second-growth and old-growth conifer forest, gaining roughly 1,900 ft over the first ~5.5-6 miles. At about 3 miles, pass the signed junction with the Tull Canyon Trail #847 (a steep 0.6-mile side spur to a 1952 B-17 crash site) and continue straight on #840. Around 0.5 mile past that junction the trail crosses Copper Creek near the historic Tubal Cain Mine tailings (last reliable, easy water before the lake), then switchbacks up through subalpine meadows toward Buckhorn Pass. Watch for the unsigned or lightly-signed spur (near ~5,200 ft, roughly 5.5-6 miles in) that drops left/southwest to Buckhorn Lake -- it's easy to miss, so watch for the left turn to Buckhorn Lake. Follow this spur down to the lake, which is the last dependable water source before the summit push. From the south end of Buckhorn Lake the maintained tread disappears; cross the inlet stream/waterfall at the head of the lake and pick up a faint boot path heading southwest into avalanche-damaged timber (expect blowdown and light bushwhacking). This opens into a broad, flat bench of avalanche debris about 200 ft above the lake -- the true start of the off-trail scramble. From there climb a wide talus/scree gully trending south then curving east, breaking treeline around 5,800 ft (roughly 700 ft above the lake), where the going turns to loose rock and light class 2-3 scrambling. Angle east/southeast up increasingly loose slopes to gain the Iron-Worthington col at approximately 6,420 ft. Hazards on this leg: avalanche debris and blowdown near the lake, sustained loose scree/talus underfoot above treeline (helmet recommended for rockfall from parties above), and route-finding through the faint, unmarked path -- a GPS track or detailed written beta is strongly advised since cairns are sparse. From the Iron-Worthington col, angle northeast up open slopes to the base of Worthington's summit fin; the final class 3 scramble drops a few feet left of the ridge crest to a short (~10 ft) crack, then follows the top of the fin to the true summit.
